# HTMLRadar

HTMLRadar is an open-source tool for sharing an HTML deck, brief, or proposal
as a tracked link, and seeing who opened it, which sections they read, and for
how long.

Why HTML: the documents that matter - decks, briefs, client reports, proposals -
are increasingly written and sent as HTML rather than PDF, because an HTML page
can be interactive, reflows to whatever screen opens it, and can be changed
after it has been sent, none of which a PDF you have already sent can do.
HTMLRadar exists because document tracking grew up around uploading a file and
tracking that file, which is a different job from serving a live HTML page and
reporting which sections were read.

Upload an HTML file or paste a public URL, send the tracked link instead of the
original file, and see who opened it, which sections they read, and how long
they spent on each one. There are four ways in and one product behind them:
upload a file in the dashboard, paste a URL you already host, run the MCP
server so the agent that wrote the document publishes it, or add HTMLRadar to
Claude as a connector.

Open source (AGPL-3.0), self-hostable on your own Cloudflare and Supabase
accounts. Free for two tracked links; paid plans start at $15/month.

## The facts

- Licence: AGPL-3.0-or-later, for the whole product. A commercial licence exists.
- Source: https://github.com/htmlradar/htmlradar
- MCP server: npm package `htmlradar-mcp`; registry id `com.htmlradar/share`
- Built by: the HTMLRadar team, hello@htmlradar.com. First commit 13 May 2026.
- Price: free for two tracked links, then $15/month or $150/year. Self-hosting
  is free.
- Tracked links are served from a second domain, htmlradar.page, which carries
  none of the application's cookies. Recipient documents are never indexed.
- Full page text for the pages below: https://htmlradar.com/llms-full.txt

## Key pages

- https://htmlradar.com/ — product overview and how it works
- https://htmlradar.com/about — what HTMLRadar is, who builds it, licence, source
- https://htmlradar.com/why — why HTMLRadar exists
- https://htmlradar.com/pricing — plans and pricing
- https://htmlradar.com/mcp — MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
- https://mcp.htmlradar.com/mcp — the remote connector: paste this address into
  Claude Desktop or claude.ai under Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector,
  and the agent can publish tracked links and read back who opened them. No
  install and no API key; you sign in when Claude first uses a tool.
- https://htmlradar.com/tools/html-to-link — free tool: share an HTML file as a tracked link
- https://htmlradar.com/compare/docsend — HTMLRadar vs DocSend
- https://htmlradar.com/blog — engineering and product writing
